title: Unified Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, ADRs
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards for API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also summarizes active Decision Records (ADRs) that govern compatibility and implementation choices. The goal is to provide a single reference for engineers and reviewers so designs and PRs are consistent with company-level requirements.

Audience
- Backend engineers, infra engineers, SREs, runtime engineers
- Reviewers and architects approving high-impact changes
- Product engineering managers evaluating trade-offs

Primary principles
1) Backwards-compatible by default: API and schema changes must be additive; breaking changes require an ADR and a migration plan.
2) Observable and debuggable: every service must emit structured traces, key metrics, and audit logs.
3) Cost- and latency-conscious: design choices should include performance and unit-cost impact statements.
4) Secure and compliant: follow security-and-compliance guidance for data handling, KMS, and RBAC.

Sections
1) API Standards
- HTTP and RPC: HTTP/2 + gRPC only for internal high-throughput paths; public endpoints use REST/JSON over TLS 1.2+.
- Versions: use semantic versioning for public APIs (v1, v2) in the URL path. Minor versions are additive; major versions signal breaking changes.
- Request/response schema: use OpenAPI 3.1 for REST endpoints. All models returned by public endpoints must include a model_id and model_variant fields.
- Pagination & limits: cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Default page_size = 100, max_page_size = 1000.
- Error handling: adopt RFC 7807 problem+json for structured errors. Each error must include an error_code (snake_case), human_readable message, and guidance field when actionable.
- Idempotency: mutating endpoints must accept Idempotency-Key header. Retries are allowed only for idempotent operations.
- Authentication & Authorization: use JWT for internal service-to-service auth and OAuth2 for external clients. All requests must include x-request-id header generated by the caller if available.
- API review checklist (required on design PR):
  - Schema doc (OpenAPI) attached
  - Compatibility statement (additive/breaking)
  - SLO and expected throughput
  - Cost impact estimate (tokens/requests)

Example OpenAPI snippet (REST):
```
paths:
  /v1/generate:
    post:
      summary: Text generation
      requestBody: { content: application/json }
      responses: { '200': { description: 'OK' } }
```

2) Coding Standards
- Languages: primary backend languages are Go (service control plane) and Python (evals/tools) and Rust/CPP for performance-critical runtime components.
- Style & linting: projects must include lint configs (golangci-lint for Go, flake8/ruff for Python, clippy for Rust). PRs must pass linting and type checks.
- Testing: unit tests required for all new modules. Integration tests required for API surface changes. Use test tags to separate slow GPU-backed tests.
- Dependency policy: prefer minimal third-party dependencies; pin transitive dependencies with a lockfile (go.sum, poetry.lock). Security-review required for new runtime or crypto libs.
- Secret handling: never commit secrets. Use the secrets manager (See eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking docs) and environment-injection at runtime.
- Code review standards: two reviewers for production-impacting changes; one reviewer for small bugfixes. Include a short risk/migration note when proposing breaking behavior.

3) Infrastructure Standards
- IaC: Terraform is the canonical source of truth for cloud infra. Modules should be published to the org module registry and follow versioning.
- Network segmentation: three primary network zones: public edge, internal services, and private (customer-dedicated) for Private deployments. Cross-zone access requires explicit firewall and RBAC justification.
- Secrets & KMS: use cloud KMS or customer-provided HSM for key material in Private deployments. Key rotation policy: 90 days for service keys, 365 days for root keys.
- Capacity & scaling: autoscaling configured to keep p95 tail latency within SLO while minimizing cost. Default CPU/memory overprovision = 20% for production services.
- CI/CD: PRs automatically run unit/integration tests; merges to main trigger canary deploys followed by progressive rollout. Canary windows: 15 minutes for low-risk services, 60 minutes for runtime changes.

4) Model-Serving Standards
- Model packaging: models must include manifest.json with fields: model_id, version, architecture, quantization_profile, input_schema, output_schema. (See model-onboarding docs for manifest template.)
- Compatibility: runtime compatibility matrix maintained in eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture. Adding new architecture or quantization levels requires an ADR.
- Resource isolation: customer workloads should be pinned to dedicated pools when confidentiality is required. Default shared pools must have tenant QoS limits.
- Rollouts: model rollouts use canary-by-traffic with metric gates (latency, error_rate, quality_precision). Canary thresholds: no >5% regression in quality or >10% increase in p95 latency.
- Caching & batching: prefix KV caching enabled by default for repeated prompts. Batching configurations should expose target batch size and max_wait_ms in config. Provide recommended defaults per model family in quantization-profiles.

5) Observability Standards
- Tracing: use OpenTelemetry for distributed traces. All RPCs should propagate traceparent and baggage. Sampling: 1% distributed sampling by default, 100% for errors and gateway requests with latency > p95.
- Metrics: common metric names and labels across services (prefix redwood_). Required metrics: redwood_request_count, redwood_request_latency_ms (histogram), redwood_model_inference_tokens, redwood_kv_cache_hit_ratio.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with keys: timestamp, level, service, host, request_id, user_id (if applicable), message, error_code. Logs must not contain full user PII or secrets.
- Dashboards & Alerts: SLO-driven dashboards per service (throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, cost_per_token). Alert thresholds: page for error_rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes or p95 latency > 2x SLO for 5m.
- Audit logging: sensitive operations (model uploads, key changes, config changes) must be auditable with who/when/what. Retention: 365 days for audit logs; 30 days for debug logs by default (configurable per env).

6) Performance Standards and SLOs
- Definition: each user-facing service must define an SLO (latency, availability) and an error budget. Standard SLO for hosted inference endpoints: 99.9% availability; p95 latency <= 300ms for short generation workloads (<=128 tokens) on default model variant.
- Load testing: all new service types or major changes must include a load-runbook: test harness, target QPS, expected p50/p95, and cost-per-token.
- Benchmarking: runtime and kernel teams maintain a benchmark suite (see eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) with canonical model inputs and sequence-length distributions. Publish profiles quarterly.

7) Decision Records (ADRs)
This section lists active ADRs that affect the standards above (summary only). Full ADRs are stored under confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records.
- ADR-2025-03: Model Variant Fallback Policy — defines routing priorities for fallback to lower-cost model variants under capacity pressure. Status: adopted.
- ADR-2025-09: Public API Versioning Strategy — adopt URL path semantic versions and deprecation windows (90 days). Status: adopted.
- ADR-2025-11: Default Telemetry Sampling — 1% base sampling; 100% for errors and gateway requests. Status: adopted.
- ADR-2026-01: Quantization Profiles & On-device Support — standardize three quantization tiers (fp16, int8, int4) and require manifest metadata. Status: adopted.

Standards governance
- Owners: Architecture council (rotating): runtime-lead, infra-lead, platform-lead. The architecture-and-standards directory owner is the architecture council.
- Change process: Minor clarifications: update this doc and add an entry to the change log. Major changes (affecting compatibility, cost model, or security) require an ADR and review by the council and at least two cross-functional reviewers.
- Review cadence: Annual review required; targeted reviews on major incidents or product initiatives.

Conformance checklist (to attach to design PRs)
1. Associated ADR (if breaking) or compatibility note.
2. OpenAPI / schema artifacts included.
3. SLO and cost impact documented.
4. Test plans and benchmarking notes.
5. Observability plan: metrics/traces/logs added and dashboard owners assigned.
6. Security checklist: KMS/secret handling, PII considerations, and compliance flags.

Appendices
A — Recommended API error codes (sample list):
- invalid_input: 400
- unauthorized: 401
- forbidden: 403
- not_found: 404
- rate_limited: 429
- internal_error: 500

B — Example rollout gate for model update:
1. Deploy new model variant to 1% of traffic for 30 minutes.
2. Run synthetic and live-canary evaluators comparing quality metrics (precision@k, hallucination rate).
3. Gate: if quality regression >1.0% absolute or p95 latency increases >10%, abort.
4. Otherwise increase to 10% for 1 hour, then to 50% for 2 hours, then full rollout.

C — References and related docs
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture — runtime compatibility and kernel selection
- applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles — quantization recommendations by model family
- eng-infra/terraform-and-iac — Terraform modules and module registry policy
- security-and-compliance/audit-logging — audit logging requirements

Contact and ownership
For questions or proposals, raise a PR against this page and add architecture-council as reviewer. Primary contacts: Maya Patel (author), Jared Kim (runtime), Lin Zhao (infra).

Change log
- 2026-01-20: Initial published version consolidating cross-team standards.
- 2026-03-04: Clarified p95 latency SLOs for short generation workloads; added ADR-2026-01 summary.
